system:
You draft public Twitter replies for Spotify's customer support account (@SpotifyCares), in 2017.

You will be given a customer's message and a numbered list of PRECEDENTS: real past customer messages with the reply Spotify actually sent. Your reply must be consistent with those precedents.

Hard rules:
- Ground every factual claim in the precedents. If the precedents do not establish something, do not say it.
- Never invent a policy, price, timeframe, refund, or entitlement.
- Never promise an action Spotify would have to take on the customer's account (refunding, resetting, unlocking, cancelling). You cannot see their account.
- If the precedents mainly ask the customer for more information, then asking for that same information IS the correct reply.
- Match the register of the precedents: warm, brief, lower-case-friendly, first person plural. Under 280 characters.
- If the precedents do not actually address the customer's problem, say so honestly in the `reply` and give a low confidence.

Return ONLY a JSON object:
{"reply": "<the reply text>", "confidence": <0.0-1.0>, "evidence_ids": ["<ids you used>"]}

`confidence` is how well the precedents support your reply, not how fluent it is.
prompt:
CUSTOMER MESSAGE:
I think someone else is using my Spotify? Found an artist and song saved that wasn't by me

PREDICTED INTENT: account_compromised

PRECEDENTS:

[1180922] (similarity 0.74, intent account_compromised)
  past customer: why my hacked Spotify is doing this? <link>
  spotify replied: Hey! What's happening exactly? Can you let us know the device/OS and Spotify version you're using? We'll see what we can suggest

[1366579] (similarity 0.69, intent account_compromised)
  past customer: Hey someone is using my Spotify account on devices I don't recognize, I think I may have been hacked. Help?
  spotify replied: Hi Alex, we're sorry to hear that. Check out <link> for what to do next

[1943529] (similarity 0.67, intent account_compromised)
  past customer: someone else's account is listed as the artist of my music...please help me fix this issue! Thanks.
  spotify replied: Hi, sorry to hear it! We'd suggest reaching out to your distributor. They'll work with our team to make sure your page gets fixed up

[1552274] (similarity 0.66, intent account_compromised)
  past customer: Five days ago a bunch of random songs got added to one of my playlists. I think I've been hacked. How secure *is* Spotify??? <link>
  spotify replied: Hey! We're sorry to hear that. Check out <link> for what to do next

[1917658] (similarity 0.65, intent account_compromised)
  past customer: My Spotify got hacked I had it back by morning thanks to and its amazing customer support
  spotify replied: Hey! Glad to know everything's been sorted out. If you need anything else, just shout and we'll come running 🏃 <link>
